clue.text: Go to pieces quickly after meal

blocks.note: to break is to go to pieces, shatter
fast means quickly

explanation.surface: Someone falls apart in a hurry once they have eaten.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' looks like it orders the pieces, but it only joins wordplay to the definition at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: The first meal of the morning, eaten after the overnight fast is broken.

clue.text: The directors sound fed up

indicators.note: sound tells us to say the word for the directors out loud and spell what we hear differently

blocks.note: a company's directors make up its board

explanation.surface: The company bosses announce that they have had enough.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone weary and lacking interest is described as tired of things, the same state as being fed up.

clue.text: Rose in elegant fashion

indicators.note: to fashion something is to shape it, so the letters are moulded into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Somebody stood up gracefully.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rose' reads as a verb, getting up elegantly, but it is the flower. Neatly, the fodder spells 'inelegant'.
explanation.definitionFit: Eglantine is the sweet briar, a wild species of rose with scented leaves.

clue.text: Organic vegetable?

blocks.note: surface reading: produce grown without chemicals
setter's reading: a vegetable named after a body organ and shaped like it

explanation.surface: Something you would buy at a health-food shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Organic' suggests pesticide-free farming; here it means 'of an organ', the kidney.
explanation.definitionFit: This pulse is called after the bodily organ whose curved shape it resembles, so it is literally an organ-like vegetable.

clue.text: One is absorbed by papers designed to inform

indicators.note: something absorbed is taken in, so one piece ends up inside the other
designed means planned out afresh, so the combined letters are laid out in a new pattern

blocks.note: taken as written
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Documents drawn up to give a person the facts they need.
explanation.definitionFit: To apprise someone is to notify them or tell them about something, a formal synonym of inform.

clue.text: Impressive seating arrangement - not hers!

indicators.note: an arrangement puts things in a fresh order, so the following letters are reordered

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A grand set of chairs, pointedly with none for the ladies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Impressive seating arrangement' reads as one phrase, but 'arrangement' is the signal and the definition stops at 'seating'.
explanation.definitionFit: Thrones are ceremonial chairs for monarchs, about as grand as places to sit can get.

clue.text: Dull way to help

blocks.note: St is the abbreviation for street, a way
aid means help

explanation.surface: A boring method of assisting someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Staid describes someone sedate, respectable and unadventurous, which is dull in character.

clue.text: Right to take legal action without being certain

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so one piece sits around the other

blocks.note: to sue is to take someone to court
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: Someone has the right to go to court even when unsure of their case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' seems to mean lacking, but here it is the old sense 'outside': SUE goes around R.
explanation.definitionFit: Being sure means having no doubt, so it is a direct synonym of certain.

clue.text: Foreign aide's remark overheard

indicators.note: something foreign is strange and unfamiliar, so these letters appear in an unfamiliar order

blocks.note: taken as written, apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: A diplomat's assistant from abroad lets slip a comment that others catch.
explanation.definitionFit: An aside is a comment spoken so as not to be heard by all, though on stage the audience does hear it.

clue.text: Wanted to embrace secretary, but didn''t have a hope!

indicators.note: an embrace wraps arms around someone, so one word wraps around another

blocks.note: desired means wanted
PA is a personal assistant, a secretary

explanation.surface: An office romance thwarted: the boss longed to hug the secretary but it was hopeless.
explanation.definitionFit: To despair is to lose all hope, so someone who despaired had no hope left.

clue.text: Regretted bringing novice on board, having taken the decision

indicators.note: bringing someone along takes them in with you, so one piece is taken into the other
someone on board is inside the vessel, so the piece sits within the word around it

blocks.note: rued means regretted
L is for learner, as on a British learner driver's L-plate

explanation.surface: A board member regrets letting a newcomer join once the vote has been taken.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On board' is part of the container signal too: the novice goes inside RUED.
explanation.definitionFit: A committee that has ruled has given a verdict, that is, reached and announced its decision.

clue.text: Pro-change, artist destroyed pictures

indicators.note: change tells us to alter the order of the short word just before it
something destroyed is wrecked, so the word before it is broken up and rebuilt

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A painter keen on reform has wrecked his own canvases.
explanation.definitionFit: Portraits are pictures of people, painted, drawn or photographed, so they are a kind of picture.

clue.text: Fine-sounding creatures are weedy specimens

indicators.note: sounding asks for words heard rather than seen, so the phrase is spoken and spelt anew

blocks.note: dandy means fine, excellent
lions are creatures, kept as they are spoken

explanation.surface: Animals that sound splendid turn out to be puny examples.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dandy lions' spoken gives the flower's name, which comes from French dent de lion, lion's tooth.
explanation.definitionFit: Dandelions are the common yellow weeds of lawns, so they are literally specimens of weed.

clue.text: Vicar bowled over by a girl

indicators.note: a thing bowled over is knocked upside down, so the word is turned back to front

blocks.note: Rev is short for Reverend, a vicar's title
taken as written

explanation.surface: The parish priest is smitten with a young woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bowled over' suggests being smitten; it is the signal to turn REV around.
explanation.definitionFit: Vera is a woman's given name, and crosswords often define first names simply as girl.

clue.text: Stops on the way

blocks.note: surface reading: places where one pauses during a journey
setter's reading: barriers that halt traffic on a road

explanation.walkthrough: 'Stops' looks like rest stops on a trip; it is things that stop vehicles, and 'the way' is the road itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Police or workers set up barriers across a road to halt vehicles, which literally stop traffic on the highway.

clue.text: Run up road to have a bite to eat, no starter

indicators.note: in a down entry or by convention, up means the word is read backwards
with no starter the first letter of the phrase is dropped

blocks.note: Rd is the abbreviation for road

blocks.clueFragment: to have a bite to eat
blocks.note: to nibble is to take small bites of food

explanation.surface: Someone dashes up the street to grab a snack, skipping the first course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Starter' looks like a first course, a nod to the meal; it means the first letter of NIBBLE goes.
explanation.definitionFit: Liquid that dribbles trickles or runs slowly, as a nose or tap may run.

clue.text: Out of shape woman takes second cake and last of bread

indicators.note: last of means only the final letter of the next word is used

blocks.note: Di, short for Diana, is a woman's name
s is the abbreviation for second
a torte is a rich layered cake
the final letter of bread

explanation.surface: A dieter going for a second slice of cake and bread ends up out of shape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Takes' only links the pieces in order. A torte is a German or Austrian cake.
explanation.definitionFit: Something distorted has been twisted or warped, so it is literally bent out of its proper form.

clue.text: Support Orson's version with extra page

indicators.note: a version is a variant form, so the letters are offered in a different order

blocks.note: taken as written, apostrophe ignored
p is the abbreviation for page, added as an extra letter

explanation.surface: Backing Orson Welles's take on a film, with a bonus page in the script.
explanation.definitionFit: A sponsor backs a person or event, often with money, so to sponsor is to support.

clue.text: Sailor set to dilute the drink

blocks.note: an old salt is an experienced sailor
to water a drink is to dilute it

explanation.surface: A sailor is about to water down his drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The drink' is slang for the sea, so it is the definition rather than a beverage.
explanation.definitionFit: The drink is informal slang for the sea, and the sea is made of briny water.

clue.text: Official set off to part of hospital

indicators.note: off means gone bad or awry, so the short word before it is jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written
a ward is a room or section of a hospital

explanation.surface: An administrator heads off towards one of the hospital wings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set off' looks like a phrasal verb, departing; it is SET with 'off' as the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A steward is an official who manages events or affairs, such as at a race meeting or in a union.

clue.text: Stop associating with striking nonconformist

blocks.note: to drop someone is to stop associating with them
workers on strike are out

explanation.surface: Someone advises cutting ties with an eye-catching rebel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Striking' seems to mean eye-catching; here it means on strike, as in 'the miners are out'.
explanation.definitionFit: A dropout is someone who rejects conventional society or abandons education, a person who refuses to conform.

clue.text: Scout leader confused when given responsibility

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter, so only that is kept

blocks.note: the opening letter of Scout
addled means muddled, confused

explanation.surface: A troop's leader gets flustered on being put in charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scout leader' looks like a person, a scoutmaster; it only means the first letter of Scout.
explanation.definitionFit: To be saddled with something is to be burdened with a duty or task, loaded like a horse.

clue.text: It's nicer out in the south-east, to be honest

indicators.note: out suggests the letters are put out of their places and scrambled
in places the scrambled letters inside the regional abbreviation

blocks.note: SE is the abbreviation for south-east
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone frankly admits the weather is better in south-east England.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Out' looks like outdoors; it is the signal to rearrange 'nicer'.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone sincere means what they say and is genuine, which is to be honest.

clue.text: Chooses new post

indicators.note: new suggests a fresh form, so the letters of the next word are remade

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone selects a different job.
explanation.definitionFit: To opt is to make a choice between alternatives, so opts is a direct synonym of chooses.

clue.text: Bulb lit up switch

indicators.note: to switch things is to swap them round, so these letters change places

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A light bulb glowing at the flick of a switch.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is all about electric light; 'Bulb' is the plant kind.
explanation.definitionFit: A tulip grows from a bulb, so the flower is named here by its underground storage organ.

clue.text: Blossom in awkward spot by river

blocks.note: a corn is a painful hard patch on the foot
crossword sense: a river is something that flows, a flow-er

explanation.surface: Someone in a tricky situation beside a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'By' joins CORN to FLOWER. Reading 'river' as flow-er, a thing that flows, is a crossword staple.
explanation.definitionFit: The cornflower is a blue-flowered plant once common in grain fields, so it is a kind of blossom.

clue.text: Quick to criticise, I would say

blocks.note: to rap is to rebuke or criticise
I'd is the contracted form of 'I would' in speech

explanation.surface: Someone admits being quick to find fault.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Say' makes the contraction natural: in speech 'I would' becomes I'd.
explanation.definitionFit: Rapid describes something happening at great speed, a plain synonym of fast or swift.

clue.text: Imitates animals

blocks.note: first meaning: copies, mimics
second meaning: primates such as gorillas

explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means copies someone's behaviour; as a plural noun it names tail-less primates like chimpanzees.

clue.text: Contact Helen when out with weird poet

indicators.note: out suggests letters thrown out of their places and mixed up
weird means strange, so the combined letters appear in an odd order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Getting in touch with Helen while she is out with a strange bard.
explanation.definitionFit: To telephone someone is to call them, a common way of getting in touch with or contacting them.

clue.text: Distressed at having to carry out dissection

blocks.note: first meaning: upset, informal adjective
second meaning: to slice into pieces, as a biology student does

explanation.surface: A squeamish student is upset at having to dissect a frog.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally, someone badly upset is said to be hurt deeply; literally, the phrasal verb means to slice into pieces.

clue.text: Fools wrongly dispute leaving it out

indicators.note: wrongly means not correctly, so the remaining letters are set in the wrong order
leaving out means omitting, so the letters of the word it are removed

blocks.note: taken as written
the letters to be removed

explanation.surface: Gullible people argue mistakenly, missing the point.
explanation.definitionFit: Dupes are people easily tricked or deceived, so the noun means fools or gullible victims.

clue.text: Valued confident entry into free trade

indicators.note: free suggests letters let loose from their order and rearranged
an entry into something goes inside it, so one piece is placed within the other

blocks.note: taken as written
sure means confident

explanation.surface: A self-assured nation joins a free-trade area and is prized for it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Free trade' reads as an economics term; 'free' is the signal to rearrange 'trade'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something treasured is cherished and held dear, so it is highly valued.
